clue.text: Ancient Peruvians facing east as a precaution

parts.note: the Incas ruled an empire in Peru before the Spanish conquest

clue.text: Encrusted Baroque stein

clue.text: Capitol is dysfunctional — it's a kind of illusion

clue.text: Dense plastic encircles large arch without limits

clue.text: Sir, I act subversively — like Jonathan Swift

clue.text: Compartment with old musical instrument

clue.text: Football formation, slanted and complex

clue.text: Smoother malefactor concealing a type of renewable energy

clue.text: Liberal leader withdraws from all-out struggle

clue.text: Blemishes rising underneath endure as fatal danger for a camel?

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the final small burden that makes an overloaded situation collapse, as with the proverbial camel.

the oil is found inside the Italian port's name

clue.text: Frantic effort to hide notice of quid pro quo

clue.text: LA personal: "eccentric with source of clean energy"

clue.text: Saint abandons loftier workshop

clue.text: Identical, as in a Chicago train

clue.text: Pen surrounding a lodge

clue.text: Doctor seated around no one with no seat

clue.text: Orchestra violinists full of Italian food
